job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: Ten-year-old Kabir and his grandfather, Mr. Rao, were walking through their lush garden in Mysore on a humid Tuesday. Kabir noticed his pet goldfish, Goldie, gulping air at the surface of the pond. 'Grandpa, is Goldie tired?' Kabir asked, thinking the fish was panting like he did after a race. Mr. Rao smiled and explained that fish use gills to extract oxygen from water. He pointed to 2 large lily pads nearby. 'Actually, Kabir, Goldie is gulping because the water temperature has risen, which lowers the amount of dissolved oxygen available for her to breathe.' They walked past 5 blooming hibiscus bushes. Kabir realized that just as he needed to breathe faster when running, Goldie needed to gulp more when her environment changed. Mr. Rao added that plants also respire, but they do it differently than animals. Kabir felt relieved knowing Goldie wasn't just lazy. He decided to add a fountain to the pond to help circulate the water. As they reached the gate, Kabir felt proud of his new knowledge about how living things survive in different conditions.
response.summary: Kabir observes his goldfish gulping air in his garden pond in Mysore. His grandfather explains that rising water temperatures reduce oxygen levels, forcing the fish to gulp more. They discuss how different living organisms manage their respiration needs.
